correctness.rationale: For any 2theta-regular graph on a recurrent orbit, excitation counts are nonincreasing, hence constant; edge saturation gives A u_t=theta(u_{t−1}+u_{t+1}) for all vertices. Discrete Fourier modes demand adjacency eigenvalues theta(zeta+zeta^−1). The nonincidence design has exact spectrum ±q²,±sqrt(q); the normalized small eigenvalues have rational square 4/q³ strictly between zero and one and therefore cannot be sums of roots of unity. Remaining ±q² frequencies imply an impossible two-periodic excited set. Independently, two exact exhaustive algorithms classify all 3^14 labelled Fano states identically, with sharp witness 82105. Verified decoded package code/results included.

value.rationale: The natural finite projective-plane nonincidence family (including possible non-Desarguesian planes) lies on the exact induced-density/half-degree equality where previous generic extinction theorems no longer apply. The new all-period spectral criterion proves universal extinction throughout that boundary family, while another same-degree, same-threshold bipartite network sustains oscillations. An independently certified sharp order-two extinction histogram supplies a concrete benchmark and shows exact relaxation profile, not merely a toy normalization.
